purpose: Check Philippine range and taxonomic context for three remaining San Agustin labels with source spelling variants.

method.scope: Focused review of Periophthalmus barbarus, Poecilia reticulata, and Oxyurichthys ophthalmonema plus the spelling variants retained from Tables 1-2 and the plate.
method.distinction: Taxonomic validity, broad range summaries, introduced-species context, and identification of the San Agustin specimens are separate claims. An out-of-range label prioritizes voucher review but does not prove absence or misidentification.
method.evidenceLimit: No voucher/accession crosswalk, diagnostic image review, or author clarification was obtained. The source spellings remain verbatim; no candidate was applied to occurrence or app data.
method.authorityAccess: Catalog of Fishes records were reviewed through indexed current-status excerpts; the Periophthalmus page returned HTTP 403 on direct open. The Smithsonian repository chapter and Plazi treatment were retrieved; the Zootaxa issue page shows the journal PDF requires subscription or fee.
method.sourceReuse: The Zootaxa issue page marks the checklist PDF as subscription/fee access. The accessible Plazi treatment supplies the concise checklist text used here; no item-specific public-app reuse permission was established.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The Table 1 name matched GBIF exactly as an accepted species. The separate spelling Periophthalmus barbarous is a GBIF synonym pointing to P. barbarus; this resolves a spelling candidate only.
findings.currentAuthority: Eschmeyer’s Catalog of Fishes lists P. barbarus as valid with an Eastern Atlantic range from Morocco south to Angola, including Gulf of Guinea islands. Murdy and colleagues’ Smithsonian-hosted mudskipper synthesis likewise describes this as the single Periophthalmus species on the tropical west African coast. FishBase flags reports from the Philippines as needing confirmation.
findings.conflict: The accepted range sources do not include the Philippines, in contrast with the San Agustin, Romblon context reported by the source article.
findings.priority: high; fifth range mismatch in this focused review
findings.action: Preserve the source name and request the RSU voucher/accession, diagnostic photographs and author confirmation. Do not infer absence, misidentification, or a corrected local occurrence from range data alone.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The Table 1 name matched GBIF exactly as accepted. The plate form Poecilia reticulate is a separate GBIF synonym mapped to P. reticulata; keep the printed variant until the source image/table is confirmed.
findings.philippinesContext: Jamandre’s 2023 provisional checklist marks P. reticulata as introduced and reports introduction to river basins across the Philippines, citing Guerrero (2014). This is broad national introduced-species context, not confirmation of the San Agustin survey specimen, reach, or current local population.
findings.disposition: No geographic outlier is flagged from this national context. Do not label the San Agustin record native, established, abundant, or current based on this cross-check.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The Table 1 name matched GBIF exactly as accepted. The possible plate/OCR form returned a fuzzy synonym suggestion for Oxyurichthys opthalmonemus; it is not a safe automatic correction.
findings.currentAuthority: Eschmeyer’s Catalog of Fishes lists O. ophthalmonema as valid and gives a broad Indo-West Pacific distribution extending east to Micronesia and Fiji. A Smithsonian NMNH record under this name is associated with a 2013 Philippines survey but gives San Jose Market, Antique as its place; market provenance is not a natural capture site or San Agustin locality.
findings.disposition: The Table 1 name is taxonomically supported, while the secondary variant remains unresolved. The separate museum record provides only contextual name/provenance evidence; no local survey occurrence is transferred.

nextAction: Continue the range and current-authority screen for the remaining 9 of 39 Table 1 labels. Keep the six range-mismatch labels and unresolved spelling variants in the voucher-verification queue; retain the Tridentiger trigonocephalus authority discrepancy separately. Do not turn national range, introduction context, or a GBIF name match into a San Agustin occurrence claim. See mimaropa-san-agustin-range-authority-followup-20261105.json.
